start._comment: The whole docs site in dev, every language, on http://localhost:3000 - English at `/`, Czech at `/cs/`, the paths the deployed site uses. The two servers behind it are continuous dependencies, so Nx starts them with this and one Ctrl-C stops all three.

start-en._comment: The English half of the dev site, on a private port behind `start`'s proxy. `.docusaurus-dev` instead of the default `.docusaurus`, because `docusaurus start` and `docusaurus build` generate into the SAME folder. A build run while the dev server is up (`nx build docs`, or anything that depends on it) overwrites that folder underneath it; the watcher sees the change and recompiles the running site from the build's leftovers - production config, and the last locale built, which is `cs`. The English dev site then believes its baseUrl is `/cs/`, so every link and every hot reload lands on a path it does not serve: a 404 in the other language, out of nowhere, on the next keystroke. Separate folders make that collision impossible - and the Czech dev server needs its own for the same reason.

start-cs._comment: The Czech half, beside the English one instead of in place of it: `docusaurus start` serves exactly one locale, so both languages at once means two servers. It serves them at the localized base path, which is what lets the proxy route by `/cs/` and what makes the links between the two work.

dev._comment: What `pnpm dev` starts for this project. One target name means "the dev servers of this project" in every project, so `nx run-many -t dev` needs no list of exceptions.

gen-json-schema._comment: The published import schema (plan §1, ADR-0014). Generated from the domain's own SETTINGS registry and SCHEMA_VERSION, so it can never describe last month's shape. Lands in static/, which Docusaurus copies to the site root — https://achordeon.eu/achordeon.schema.json, one stable URL with no version in the path.

gen-ui-strings._comment: The app labels the docs quote, pulled from the app's own translation tables by id (`<Ui id="…">`). Inputs cover both the source of the words and the pages that ask for them, so adding a quote to an .mdx re-runs it.

clear._comment: Both generated folders: `docusaurus clear` only knows about the one it is pointed at, and the dev server's (see `start`) is exactly the one somebody reaches for `clear` to unstick.

commands: node -e "for (const d of ['apps/docs/.docusaurus-dev', 'apps/docs/.docusaurus-dev-cs']) require('node:fs').rmSync(d, { recursive: true, force: true })"
